### Blessed Be Abram
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/blessed-be-abram
Passage: Genesis 14:18-20
Points:
- Melchizedek’s name and royal city of Salem highlight his righteous character and association with divine peace.
- By blessing Abram and serving God Most High, Melchizedek combines the offices of prophet, priest, and king.
- Offering bread and wine demonstrates generous hospitality and reflects God’s faithfulness to bless Abram.
- Abram’s acceptance of the blessing acknowledges that the one true God gave him victory over his enemies.
- Abram’s tithe models genuine worship and stewardship by supporting those who minister on God's behalf.

### Read the Bible: Genesis 14, Matthew 13, Nehemiah 3, and Acts 13
Author: D. A. Carson
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/devotionals/read-the-bible/genesis-14-matthew-13-nehemiah-3-acts-13/
Passage: Genesis 14:18-20
Points:
- Abram refuses riches from the wicked king of Sodom but gladly receives blessing from Melchizedek.
- Melchizedek reveals that Abram was not alone in knowing and serving the living God Most High.
- Melchizedek's peaceful city of Salem serves as a spiritual contrast to the worldly corruption of Sodom.
- Appearing without recorded genealogy, Melchizedek mysteriously enters the Genesis narrative as a unique historical figure.
- The encounter establishes a vital biblical type foreshadowing Jesus Christ as the ultimate eternal priest-king.
